message.content:
This is a CBP ruling on Piracema White, a gneiss slab. Gneiss is classified as "other monumental or building stone" in heading 6802. Heading 6802 covers worked monumental or building stone, while heading 2515 covers marble, travertine and similar calcareous stone, and 2516 covers granite, porphyry, basalt, sandstone and other monumental or building stone. Gneiss is not calcareous, so it is not under 2515.

In 6802, subheading 6802.91 covers marble, travertine and alabaster. 6802.92 covers other calcareous stone. 6802.93 covers granite. 6802.99 covers other stone. Gneiss is not granite in the tariff sense unless it is treated as such under the chapter's definitions. Chapter 25 and 68 notes treat granite broadly in commerce, but CBP lab analysis says gneiss, so 6802.99 is the likely heading. Within 6802.99, the 10-digit codes are 6802.99.0010 for "Other: Slabs" and 6802.99.0090 for "Other".

Alternatively, 6802.10 covers tiles, cubes and similar articles with a largest surface area under 7 cm. That does not apply here. The slabs are polished on top, so they are worked beyond simply cut, which puts them in 6802 rather than 2516.

I recall the ruling classified the slabs in 6802.99.0090 or 6802.93, and I am not certain which. Because the stone is gneiss rather than granite, I choose 6802.99. The statistical suffix is uncertain. The 6802.99.00 line has 10-digit breakouts of 6802.99.0010 "Other stone: Slabs" and 6802.99.0090 "Other", so I choose 6802.99.0090 as the best fit.

{"hts_code": "6802.99.0090", "reason": "Polished-top gneiss slabs are worked monumental or building stone of heading 6802, and since gneiss is neither calcareous nor granite, they fall in the 'other stone' subheading 6802.99."}
